The three buttons below the right list change between groups and modpacks. They let you include active mods, prepare activation or capture, and manage contents or exceptions. Read their labels and review any confirmation before proceeding.
Back returns to your saved modpacks; Close hides the library. Both preserve drafts during this session. Use Save library to keep edits across sessions.

Select visible selects rows from the current filter for bulk actions. Add selected and Remove selected change their membership in the group or modpack. Row selection and membership checkboxes serve different purposes.
New opens a name entry dialog. In Groups, Subgroup creates one inside the selection. In Modpacks, the second button duplicates an entry. Close or cancel the naming dialog before using other actions.

Rows show mods or groups and their membership in the selected entry. The checkbox changes that membership. Click selects rows; Ctrl and Shift extend selection for bulk actions. Dependencies are resolved when preparing a load.
Rename changes the selected entry name. Delete removes that library entry after the relevant check; it does not uninstall Workshop mods. Save the library to retain edits.

Save library stores this organisation. If another window has changed the same data, a conflict is reported and you can reload before overwriting it. This save is separate from Apply changes in the manager and does not reload Lua.
Search the library to locate what you want to edit. Filtering does not delete entries or change active mods. Select a group or modpack on the left to inspect its contents.
These tabs separate reusable groups from modpacks. A group contains mods and can have subgroups; a modpack combines groups with exceptions. Switching tabs retains draft edits.
This menu offers comparison, history and moving groups. These tools organize the library. Save stores the library; Apply changes commits game configuration.
This list shows your groups or modpacks. The right side follows the selected entry. Several modpacks can use the same group; consider that shared scope before changing its contents.

Apply changes commits active mods and their prepared order to the game. Declared incompatibilities show a warning with Apply anyway and Close. Accepting continues with both mods selected; Close cancels the application. Missing dependencies and other blocking errors are checked separately. This step may reload Lua.

The left column lists installed mods. Ctrl + click adds or removes mods from the selection without enabling them. In Categories, drag a selected row to another category to move the selection. In Complete with Roomy rows, use a selected row's category picker. Esc clears the selection. Toggles and favourites act on their own mod.

The notepad and pencil opens Organise categories. Select a category to change its name or icon, create another, and adjust their order. Buttons 1 to 6 in the Type row change the icon style in both lists and remember your choice. You can move and resize the window; finish with Save and close.

Layout lets you choose Automatic, two or three columns. Automatic adapts to the available space. In two columns, use View details to open a mod's details; in three, its details occupy the middle column. Changing layout preserves profiles and load order.

Open detailed modpack management with bulk selection, comparison, revisions, import and export. Composer edits remain in their draft; save them before editing the same modpack in another view. Groups has a permanent tab above.

Capture active takes the selection and order prepared in the right column as the modpack basis. Use it to preserve a list you have already organised. Check the name and save the composition when ready.

Close hides the library; you can reopen it during the session. Drafts do not replace saving. Drag the header to move the window; the manager behind it stays usable while no confirmation or tutorial is open.

The list starts with included groups. Add groups shows available groups; Show included returns to modpack contents. Toggle a group to include or remove it. Select its name to change its priority with Up and Down.

This button calculates the composition selection and shows relevant changes and dependencies before confirmation. Loading prepares the manager list. Apply changes in the manager remains the step that commits game configuration.

The list starts with included mods and their dependencies. Add mods shows available mods to customize the selection. Click a mod to include or exclude it; an automatic dependency is removed by removing the mods that require it.

This name identifies the composition you will save. A modpack combines reusable groups with individual inclusions or exclusions. It differs from a visual category: it stores a selection you can load again.
New modpack starts another composition. If you have unsaved changes, a confirmation appears before replacing the draft. Saved modpacks are preserved.
Select a group and use Up or Down to prepare its priority in this composition. This does not change its contents. Loading the modpack resolves declared dependencies, which keep their load priority.

For a saved modpack, Review groups lets you inspect changes to its included groups. You can assess a group update before adopting it in that profile. This action is unavailable until a profile has been saved.
Save modpack saves the open composition. Save a copy creates another modpack with the entered name. Saving never activates mods in the game or reloads Lua.

This selector changes catalogue row size: Compact, Normal or Roomy. Compact shows more mods; Normal leaves space for the category; Roomy lets you change it from the row. It applies to both the complete and category views.

The details show images, description, status and an editable category. Incompatibilities shows declarations from mods, with icons and hover information; this is not a complete compatibility analysis. You can accept incompatibilities with Apply anyway. Dependencies retain their links and switches.

Select a catalogue mod to display its central details. The page contains description, images, source and dependencies, with links and switches. The guide currently highlights the list because no details page is visible yet.

Select a mod and click View details. Its description, images and dependencies open in a movable window. Links and switches work as in three columns. Close the window with its button or Escape to see the full list again.

This button sits at the bottom of the catalogue. Before changing the selection, a confirmation shows the affected mods. DMM checks declared dependencies when enabling or disabling mods; it cannot detect every code conflict between mods.

Discard and exit abandons selection changes you have not applied; it does not delete saved profiles. Close this guide to use the controls. Reopen it through Tools, jump to a step with the dropdown, and navigate with arrow keys or Escape.

This dropdown contains All, Active, Inactive, With warnings, Local and Favourites. Choosing another filter leaves Favourites. With warnings filters the catalogue; warnings affecting active mods are also available in Tools when present.
Search by name or ID and filter by category. All shows the full catalog and In this group shows its members. Changing filters does not change contents.
Only checkboxes add or remove mods. Clicking a name selects the row. Icons come from the mod lists. Inherited members are edited in their source subgroup.
Enter a name. Saved or Unsaved refers to this group. Changes remain in the editor until you save them.
Undo reverts the last edit. Save group stores its name and members without activating mods or applying game changes. Leaving with changes lets you save, discard or keep editing.
New group opens the editor directly. From selection captures the mods prepared in the load-order panel. Neither action activates mods.
Edit group opens one checklist. Delete asks for confirmation and preserves copies saved in modpacks.
Select a group from the list. The right panel shows its saved contents; clicking a mod here does not change group membership.
The list shows the modpack contents and each mod origin: a group, an individual addition or a dependency. Search by name or ID. Missing mods are marked; inspecting contents never toggles activation.
New modpack opens an empty composition. Create from selection copies the selection and order staged in the right column without applying changes to the game.
Edit opens the selected modpack in its editor. The home screen is read-only; Duplicate is in More options. Move the window by its header and resize it from the right or bottom edge.

Review and load opens a preview of activation, deactivation and order changes. Confirming stages the selection in the manager. Only Apply changes saves game configuration. Incompatibilities show a warning you can explicitly accept.
This dropdown offers Duplicate, Compare, History and Delete. It opens beside the button and closes on an outside click or Escape. Deletion always asks for confirmation.
This button becomes available when the modpack groups have pending changes. Choose which updates to include and inspect the result before accepting. Modpacks never update automatically.

Search by name and select a modpack to inspect its contents. The summary shows mod and group counts. A pending notice means an original group changed; the modpack keeps its snapshot until you review those changes.
Modpacks shows saved selections. Groups manages reusable collections. Switching tabs preserves open drafts; save edits you want to keep across sessions.
Choose a step to jump to it. Arrow keys: previous/next. Escape: close. Scroll if the text does not fit.

Open the Modpack Library to create, edit and duplicate your profiles. Choose one in the selector and use Load profile to prepare its selection. ✓ marks the loaded profile and * indicates changes. Save profile in the load-order panel saves your selection; Apply changes confirms the game configuration.
Search by name or ID and filter by category. All shows the catalog; In this modpack shows included mods and required dependencies. Filters do not change contents.

Add group includes a snapshot of a saved group. Drag chips to change priority, or select a chip and press Left or Right. The x removes a group from this modpack without deleting it from the library. The buttons beside the chips show groups that do not fit.
Only the checkbox adds or excludes a mod. Clicking the name selects the row. Source identifies a group, an individual addition or a dependency. A lock marks components required by other mods.
Enter the modpack name. Saved and Unsaved refer to this draft, not to the game configuration.
This dropdown offers adding a group, saving a copy, capturing the selection, comparison and history. Tools requiring a saved modpack review pending edits first.
Undo reverts recent name, mod and group edits. Save modpack stores the draft without activating mods or reloading Lua. Leaving with changes lets you save, discard or keep editing.

The original presets offer Save, Delete and New. New creates a preset from the staged selection; Save updates the selected preset. They are separate from DMM modpacks. Loading reviews changes; only Apply changes commits game configuration.

New shows the five latest additions without replacing their real categories. Click a name to locate its mod, the dropdown to reassign it or the switch to enable it. History contains up to 50 additions and has its own Compact/Normal/Roomy selector; Roomy allows category changes, with no activation controls. Collapse/Expand and Top float at the upper right of the list.

Undo restores the available previous state. Collapse/Expand makes active categories easier to browse. Search above this column filters its contents without disabling mods or removing the prepared order.

The right column contains active mods. Ctrl + click adds or removes mods from the selection. Drag a selected row to move the group, preserving relative order and dependency priority. Moving does not apply configuration or reload Lua: the order stays prepared until saved or applied.

The Categories bar opens the same editor as the catalogue. Click a header to collapse or expand it; drag it to reorder both lists and move its active mods as a block. Dependencies retain priority. Category positions are saved; mod load order remains staged until saved or applied. The disk icon captures the category as a reusable group.

Recently added opens the session history of activations and deactivations. This differs from New, which shows recorded installations. The history is a movable window that lets you keep using the manager.

Green means the selection and order match the reference profile. Red means that profile has unsaved differences. Grey means there is no reference profile. Hover over the light for its state. This light does not mean you have applied changes to the game.

Save profile stores the prepared selection and order in a modpack, or updates the selected one. You can keep organising afterwards. This save does not commit game configuration or reload Lua. An unchanged profile needs no duplicate save confirmation.
Saving a profile does not apply changes
Search by part of a name, ID or author. Search combines with the selected filter and works in both the complete and category views. Clear the search to restore the filter results.

This dropdown sorts the catalogue, for example by name, recent additions or update date. Last updated refers to the Steam Workshop publication update, not its download. Sorting the catalogue does not change the load order in the right column.

Choose how DMM looks. You can try the icons here with the mouse. On keyboard, use the arrows and Enter to choose a theme; Tab switches between the palette and tutorial navigation. On controller, use the D-pad and A to choose; LB/RB change steps. You can close the guide at any time. Themes remain available under Tools → Themes.

Tools lets you change themes, open the tutorial, copy IDs and Workshop text, and review warnings. Debug is off by default. Enable it before reproducing an issue: Debug folder then updates the report and opens Zomboid/Lua. Click outside to close the menu.
Return to Tools whenever you need

These two icons switch between the complete list and categories. Categories and assignments are shared with the right column. Drag a header to move the whole category in both lists; a short click collapses or expands it. The catalogue shows filtered results; the right column shows active mods. Your view and collapsed categories are remembered after restarting.
History row size, independent of the catalogue. Roomy lets you change the category.
